whatIs.title: What is a startup? Who is a founder?
whatIs.subtitle: Here’s the simple version — no jargon, just everyday language

startup.title: What is a startup?
startup.body: A startup isn’t just a business. It’s an idea that solves a real problem in a new way — quickly and affordably. It starts small, with a sketch in a notebook or a note on your phone. What matters is that it makes someone’s life easier in some way.

founder.title: Who is a founder?
founder.body: A founder is someone who doesn’t sit around waiting for a diploma or big investment. They spot a problem around them and say, “I’ll solve this.” Whether you’re in school, at university or still finding your way — it doesn’t matter. The only requirement is the courage to start.

now.title: Why now?
now.body: Because experience comes from doing, not from books. Here you can test an idea, get real feedback and find a team — all in one place, and for free. The best time is always now.

doubts.title: Why shouldn’t you start today?
doubts.subtitle: Here are the four most common reasons you tell yourself. Open each one and answer honestly: which of them is really worth stopping for?

simple.a: Even the biggest products started with one simple idea. What matters isn’t how big the idea is, but that you pick it up and try it. Share your idea here, get feedback and find out from real people whether it’s truly worth it.

formula.question: How are rankings calculated?
formula.intro: Ratings use a 10-point scale. A simple average would be unfair: a startup with a single 10 would jump ahead of one averaging 9.6 across 1,000 votes. That’s why, like IMDb’s Top 250, we use a Bayesian (weighted) rating — when there are few votes, the score is “pulled” toward the overall average.
